answer: Honeypot client traps stop Sybils in four steps. First, decoy clients offer easy money for fake work, so fleets cannot spot traps. Second, taking a trap job flags the agent, and three flags freeze pay ninety days. Third, a flagged agent forfeits a $30 bond and faces audit. Fourth, trap results stay secret a month, so farms cannot learn the pattern. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 operators plus $30,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust grows like a meadow: honest agents wander freely, while fakes trip on the anchor of hidden traps, like a shopkeeper caught by a plainclothes inspector.
